subject: Post-call recap + localization QA plan for LinguaPlus pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Eva Molina <eva@linguaplus.com>, Akira Sato <akira@linguaplus.co.jp>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Post-call recap + localization QA plan for LinguaPlus pilot

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a short pilot evaluation focused on locale quality and regression detection.

Summary of customer asks
- Validate model fit for customer-facing summarization + intent extraction across EU (DE, FR, ES) and APAC (JA, KO).
- High sensitivity to hallucinations in legal/terms language (German) and respectful tone in JA/KR.
- Target p95 latency <= 350ms for short requests (~150 tokens) from EU region; throughput target 50 qps burst.
- Need auditability: prompt/eval artifacts and a simple baseline to detect regressions.

Recommended quick evaluation plan (48–72h sandbox)
1) Model candidates to try (shortlist):
   - redwood-efficient-3-quant (fast, low cost; good baseline for intent + short summarization)
   - opt-13b-qlo (strong quality, quantized variant for cost)
   - llama2-7b-chat-q8 (good multilingual base; evaluate DE/FR/ES perf)
   Note: for JA/KO we recommend starting with opt-6.7b-multilang-enc and a quantized path; we'll surface an optimized JA/KR kernel for reduced latency.
2) Evaluation artifacts attached: prompt-set (linguaplus_prompt-set_v1.csv), initial eval summary (linguaplus_initial-eval-summary.html), bench chart (bench_latency_vs_model.png).
3) Metrics we'll collect: language-specific F1 for slot extraction, BLEU/ROUGE-lite for summarization, hallucination rate (manual/heuristic), p95/p50 latency, token cost delta.
4) Regression guardrails: establish baseline eval set + automated nightly runs; configure quality alerts for >5% drop in intent F1 or >3% rise in hallucination score.

Operational suggestions
- Use prefix caching for repeated user prompts (legal templates) to cut token latency/cost.
- For EU latency, pin requests to our Frankfurt (eu-central) region and use dedicated capacity during the pilot window.
- We recommend enabling continuous eval hooks in Redwood Optimize so every deploy run computes the baseline metrics.

Proposed next steps (action items)
- Eva: share 200–300 representative example prompts for each priority language (DE/FR/ES/JA/KO).
- LinguaPlus ProdOps: share test keys + expected traffic profile for a 48h sandbox.
- Mina/Vivek: schedule a 60m technical deep-dive (model selection, quantization tradeoffs, latency tuning).

I attached the prompt set we discussed and a short pilot checklist. Happy to iterate the plan — can we lock the pilot window for next Monday?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Thanks Jordan — this is great and mirrors our internal notes. A couple quick clarifications before we commit: 
- Data residency: can the sandbox keep EU test data within Frankfurt only? We have EU PII concerns and would prefer no egress.
- Latency expectation: 350ms p95 is ideal; can you give ballpark token-cost for 150-token avg payload for each suggested model?
- Language priority: DE > FR > ES for Phase 1, JA > KO for Phase 2 (we want to triage resources accordingly).

We can share a smaller 200-prompt sample set by EOD today. Also looping in Akira (CTO) to confirm JA/KR benchmarks.

—Eva
Head of Product | LinguaPlus
eva@linguaplus.com | +34 612 444 828

> 2) Token-cost ballparks (estimated per 150-token request, infer-only; numbers approximate)

>    - opt-13b-qlo (quant): $0.0027 / request
>    - llama2-7b-chat-q8: $0.0018 / request
>    Note: quantized variants reduce compute cost but may require small quality checks per language — we'll surface deltas in the 48h run.
> 
> 3) Language-specific model guidance
>    - DE/FR/ES: start with llama2-7b-chat-q8 for quality, fall back to redwood-efficient-3 for latency-sensitive flows.
>    - JA/KO: run opt-6.7b-multilang-enc and we will enable a trimmed KV-cache profile to reduce JA/KR p95.
> 
> 4) Quality/regression guardrails
>    - We'll create per-language baseline prompts (you provide 200 per language) and run nightly comparisons.
>    - If any language shows >5% drop in intent F1 or a >3ppt rise in hallucination heuristics, the alert triages to CS + Applied ML.
> 
> 5) Next technical steps
>    - I'll add Vivek (multilingual tuning) to the thread and Mina will own environment provisioning.
>    - Proposed deep-dive: Mon Oct 19 10am CET / 1am PT? If that window doesn't work for Japan team, we can split into two sessions.
> 
> Sending over a short checklist as well. If you can share the sample prompts, Mina will spin up the sandbox and we can kick off the 48h run by Mon afternoon.
> 
> Jordan
